title: The O Antiphons (17–23 December)
hookLine: O Wisdom, O Root of Jesse, O Key of David, O Dayspring: the verses behind O Come, O Come Emmanuel

cards: A slow, slightly haunting tune turns up every December in churches, school concerts and shopping malls: O come, O come, Emmanuel.
Behind its English words is something far older, sung in Latin in monastery choirs on the darkest evenings of the year: seven short chants, each beginning with the same sound, O.
For many centuries, monks and nuns have sung them one a night in the last week before Christmas. A countdown, in seven names.

teach.b: An antiphon is a short verse sung before and after a psalm or canticle.
From December 17 to 23, at Evening Prayer, the Church sings a special one around Mary's song, the Magnificat, and each begins with O, a cry of longing.
Each calls the coming Christ by a different name from the Old Testament. O Wisdom. O Adonai, the Lord who spoke to Moses in the burning bush.
O Root of Jesse, from Isaiah's shoot springing from a stump. O Key of David, who opens and no one shuts. O Dayspring, the rising dawn.
O King of the nations. And last, O Emmanuel, from Isaiah 7, in the Douay-Rheims: "Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel." God with us.
Now the hidden detail. Write down the seven Latin titles, Sapientia, Adonai, Radix, Clavis, Oriens, Rex, Emmanuel, and read their first letters backward.

teach.h: ERO CRAS: TOMORROW I WILL BE.
teach.b: You get ero cras: tomorrow, I will be there. Whether a medieval monk planted that on purpose, nobody can prove. But on December 23 the last antiphon is sung, and the next night is Christmas Eve.
In 1851 the Anglican priest John Mason Neale translated a Latin hymn built on these antiphons, and later revisions of his English became the carol.
So when a mall speaker plays O come, O come, Emmanuel, it's carrying, faintly, the evening prayer of monasteries: seven names, each one a door Advent knocks on.

how: From December 17 to 23, the Liturgy of the Hours sings one O Antiphon each evening with the Magnificat, and the same antiphons serve as the Gospel acclamation at Mass on those days.

games.q: it's December 23. the monastery has sung six O antiphons. tonight is the last. which name is it?
games.why: O Emmanuel, God with us, from Isaiah 7. the next night is Christmas Eve.

practice: Choose the name that fits where you are tonight: O Wisdom, if you need to decide something; O Key, if something feels locked; O Dayspring, after a dark stretch; O Emmanuel, if you feel alone.
Say it slowly with the O in front, and let the O be the whole of it, a sound of longing. If you pray, add the old ending, come; if not, just let the name sit with you.

wordCard.voice: O Antiphons. Seven chants sung at Evening Prayer from December 17 to 23, each calling the coming Christ by an Old Testament name. Today's word.
